title: Minimax Interval Length for Fused Cohort and Case-Control Risk Differences under Vector Bias
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded delivered tier subfield below field floor (paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4); no bounded in-scope repair; panel dependency and critical-radius findings remain unrepaired.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope.
The advertised full-versus-best-scalar comparison remains an approximability result: the worked three-dimensional bracket starts at zero and does not establish a strict compression loss.
The optimized nonlinear fixed-length comparison is also open, and no executed outward-rounded certificate is supplied.
proof_attempt_summary: The run developed a local Gaussian connected-interval minimax program, finite-program certification route, and causal transfer argument, then tried to certify a strict advantage of the full vector over the best scalar projection. The worked three-dimensional bracket did not prove a positive gap or provide an executed outward-rounded certificate; D0.5 graded the result subfield, below the field floor. The panel also left a circular dependency in feasible attainment and a missing critical-radius sensitivity analysis unresolved, so the archived note is not a clean accepted proof.
tldr: Complementary cohort, target-case, and target-control samples identify a causal risk difference efficiently under exact alignment, while local control-composition error yields a bounded vector bias. The all-procedure Gaussian reduction targets the minimax maximal expected length of randomized connected intervals. For every regular Gaussian instance with fixed finite \(d\), a deterministic outward-rounded construction now gives arbitrarily tight rational brackets for both the full-vector frontier and the best scalar-projection frontier, using an exact projective net, a deterministic common nuisance mesh, directed dual lower certificates, validated primal upper certificates, and explicit continuum repair. The existing legal heterogeneous \(d=3\) example has a rigorous computable value bracket and feasible projected benchmark, but no strict full-vector advantage is currently certified. In \(d=1\), full and projected frontiers coincide. MissAdapt is only a prospective software consumer; no claim is made that it currently supports vector bias or these causal sources.
gap: Published fusion theory gives exact-alignment efficiency, local-misspecification theory gives bias-aware affine intervals and Gaussian vector-bias decision problems, and confidence-set theory gives generic duality and finite-game approximations. None certifies that the full auxiliary vector strictly outperforms every optimally selected scalar projection for arbitrary nonlinear randomized connected intervals, then transfers the full-vector frontier to all honest procedures in this three-source causal experiment.
fill: The paper proves the all-procedure endpoint-kernel reduction, constructs convergent continuum certificates, and at an explicit \(d=3\) causal baseline combines a full-vector primal with direction-net projected duals and analytic continuity bounds to certify a positive rational separation. Uniform multinomial lower transfer and pilot-selected feasible attainment preserve the causal interpretation, while optimized bounded nonlinear fixed-length inference is retained as a secondary benchmark.
